editorial_contributions.text: Summary: For our purposes, a graph is a relational structure \(\langle V,E\rangle\) where \(E\) is an irreflexive symmetric binary relation on \(V\). A graph is strongly rigid if the clone \(\text{Pol }E\) is the clone of projections. It is projective if the only idempotent operations in \(\text{Pol }E\) are projections. We show that a graph is projective if and only if the idempotent binary operations in \(\text{Pol }E\) are conservative. Other criteria are given for finite graphs. These results are used to construct large families of strongly rigid graphs. The smallest strongly rigid graph is described.
